title: Resolve one accepted Attachment receipt to reverified protected local bytes

requirements.invariant: Inside an already-open Account runtime, one complete immutable AttachmentLocalDurabilityReceipt resolves to its exact protected local bytes only after queue evidence and ciphertext independently reverify; local bytes remain the display source before upload.
A backend-neutral exact-receipt byte-resolution port accepts no Attachment-ID-only shortcut and exposes no PowerSync, database, filesystem, URL, cryptographic-key, upload or remote-storage type.

Namespace mismatch is rejected before row lookup; unknown, rebound, malformed, missing, corrupt, link-substituted or wrong-key evidence returns one bounded non-sensitive failure and never returns bytes from another environment, Principal, Account, parent or Attachment.

Resolution is one finite runtime lease: close admits no later resolution, waits for an admitted lookup/decryption to unwind before closing the attachment database or releasing the vault, and cancellation cannot return payload or strand close.

Resolution is read-only and non-consuming: it does not change queue count/order/state, create ps_crud or upload work, mark remote success, detach, delete, discard, clean up, retain, evict or choose a renderer or derivative.

This technical implementation operates only after an Account runtime is already open and grants no right to open or retain that runtime; A-016 remains the production-facing activation gate and prevents this slice from claiming authorization or user-facing release readiness.

All proof uses disposable local target fixtures and synthetic bytes; no Postgres, RLS, Data API, Sync Stream, Supabase Storage, hosted PowerSync/Auth, Firebase, production data, migration, release or cutover state changes.

items: Add AttachmentLocalByteResolving in LedgerTargetCore with the complete AttachmentLocalDurabilityReceipt as its only lookup authority and Data as its success value.

Expose stable scope-mismatch, not-found, receipt-mismatch, malformed-evidence, missing-bytes, corrupt-bytes and local-read-unavailable failures with non-sensitive diagnostic codes; ordinary Swift cancellation remains control flow rather than a domain success/failure.
No AttachmentID-only resolver, remote fallback, URL, path, provider handle or implicit current-selection lookup exists.

items: The store rejects receipt namespace mismatch before database lookup, validates the exact queue row and complete persisted receipt equality, then delegates AEAD/count/SHA reverification to the existing protected vault.
Two accepted receipts may be resolved out of FIFO order without substitution; success and failure leave queue state, count, order and pending upload evidence unchanged.
Close/reopen in the identical namespace and with the identical keys resolves the same receipt byte-identically; another namespace or key cannot do so.
The Account lifecycle owner wraps resolution in its existing finite lease and closes the attachment database only after every admitted resolution unwinds.
Reuse the existing descriptor-relative bounded ciphertext read, AES-GCM authenticated metadata, byte-count and SHA-256 reverification unchanged.
Expose no path, locator, key, URL, cache policy, renderer, derivative, upload, deletion or retention operation.
Add only one narrow public runtime facade method for an already-open Account runtime; no AppModel, SwiftUI, MCP resource/tool, current-parent lookup or user-facing authorization claim.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: No source attachment, Firebase URL/path/object or production data is read or transformed.

items: Failures expose bounded codes only; receipt IDs, parent IDs, paths, bytes, hashes, keys, SQL and provider details are absent from diagnostics and logs.
Implementation is confined to the two owned contract leaves plus the frozen shared attachment store/runtime/tests/environment-check touchpoints.
A-003/A-004/A-016, O-023 and SPIKE-MED-001 remain unadvanced; the implementation is not production/user-facing authorization.

verification.expected: Provider-free contract values and the real store resolve the requested second of two distinct receipts byte-exactly, never substitute FIFO work, and leave count/order/state unchanged.
Close/reopen with the identical scope and keys resolves the pre-close receipt to identical bytes without consuming or reordering pending evidence.

Cross-environment, Principal and Account receipts reject before lookup; unknown same-scope receipt, same-ID independently valid changed receipt and malformed/null/rebound queue evidence return their exact bounded failures and no bytes.

Missing, truncated/tampered, symlink/hardlink-substituted, wrong-key and changed count/digest/fingerprint evidence returns no bytes and does not mutate queue count/order/state or remote work. Deterministically injected database lookup and vault storage-read failures return exact localReadUnavailable with diagnostic code attachment_local_byte_read_unavailable rather than leaking provider errors.

A normally bootstrapped public LedgerOfflineClientRuntime captures two distinct Attachments and resolves the requested second receipt to its exact bytes rather than FIFO work. A gated admitted resolution holds one finite lease; concurrent close cannot begin either database close until resolution unwinds, then closes attachment before structured storage.
Cancellation returns no payload and releases the lease; reads started after closing begins or after terminal close refuse, repeated close is stable, and the facade never bypasses the lifecycle owner.

verification.owner: Ledger target source inspection, environment check and complete Swift tests
verification.expected: No AttachmentID-only API, raw store/vault/database/path/key/URL exposure, sensitive diagnostic, queue mutation, ps_crud write, remote fallback, upload, renderer, delete or retention behavior exists.

Exact implementation and promotion commits pass conversion controls, complete nonparallel Swift/MCP tests, disposable local Supabase tests, both staging builds and clean artifacts without hosted, Firebase, migration, production or cutover access.

notes: Implementation is based on exact clean commit f71e75a9c15091a45fb10727d1ec78a27d6f2fc5 after independent READY review returned GO with no P0-P3 finding. The two owned leaves now contain the backend-neutral contract and tests; frozen shared touchpoints SWIFT-F850F907B87F, TEST-CE5D3D0516D1, SWIFT-75CFE285AF37, TEST-8D6A15063B2D, SWIFT-548A8A928FAE and CONFIG-81235587F306 implement exact scope-first receipt resolution, protected-byte reverification, lifecycle drainage and public-surface containment. Executable review found and closed three P2 issues: helper cancellation preservation, proof of scope refusal before every database access and equal-length AEAD tampering with unchanged queue and ps_crud state. Final re-review is GO with no remaining P0/P1/P2. Complete local gates pass: 577 Swift tests in 91 suites, 374 pgTAP assertions in 11 files, strict database lint, 26 MCP tests, conversion/query/environment/contracts controls and both staging builds. The first parallel iOS/macOS build attempt hit their shared DerivedData lock; serial iOS rerun passed. This target-local prerequisite remains below verified until exact immutable CI passes, and remains non-production-facing while A-016 is unresolved.
